title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 168
paragraphs: The Libyans have their settlements as follows. Starting from Egypt, the first Libyans are the Adyrmachidae, who practice for the most part the same customs as the Egyptians, but wear clothing similar to that of the other Libyans. Their women wear a bronze ring on each leg and have long hair on their heads; when they catch their lice, each woman bites her own in retaliation and then throws them away. Of all the Libyans these are the only ones who do this; and they alone present their maidens to the king when they are about to be married, and whichever one of them pleases the king is deflowered by him. These Adyrmachidae extend along the coast from Egypt as far as the harbor called Plynus.
